correctness.rationale: For all integers n>=1 and x in [0,1], couple K~Bin(n,x) and U~Bernoulli(x) independently and set X=K/n,Y=(K+U)/(n+1). The expected absolute displacement is exactly 2x(1-x)/(n+1), giving the Lipschitz upper bound. The explicitly defined interlacing tent spline has f(Y)-f(X)=|Y-X| on every coupling atom, proving equality for all x and the global maximum at x=1/2. At interior x, full support forces saturation of every adjacent interlaced grid interval with one common sign; saturation plus Lipschitz continuity uniquely fixes the whole spline up to sign and constant. The same coupling and potential prove the W1 identity. Exact rational checks verify 184 (n,x) combinations via polynomial and independent cumulative-mass methods; no inference from finite checks to all degrees.

value.rationale: The natural question of stability under degree refinement has an exact sharp O(1/n) answer and a pointwise profile, sharper than generic O(n^-1/2) separate Bernstein approximation bounds on the Lipschitz class. One explicit tent spline norms the entire parameter family, and equality at just one interior point rigidly identifies that spline up to sign and constants. This controls a canonical approximation process and gives exact adjacent-binomial W1 transport, rather than a renaming or arbitrary sampled invariant.
